IBNMUJAHID:v1p543/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p543/r3.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p543/r3.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read لتنذر with tāʾ; all others read لينذر with yāʾ.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p543/r3.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر ﴿ لتنذر ﴾ بالتاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r11.claim: The warning may be addressed to Muhammad about the living, or the Qur'an itself may warn them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r11.anchor: لتنذر يا محمد من كان حيا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r13.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r13.claim: The living person has an alert heart and sight.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r13.anchor: من كان حي القلب حي البصر ، قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r14.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r14.claim: The living person is a believer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r14.anchor: من كان مؤمنا ، قاله يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r15.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r15.claim: The living person is someone guided.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r15.anchor: الرابع : من كان مهتديا , قاله السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p29/r16.claim: The decree of punishment becomes due against unbelievers.

TABATABAI:36:66-83/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r4.speaker: علي عليه السلام
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r4.claim: A report attributed to Ali interprets 'whoever is alive' as whoever is rational.
TABATABAI:36:66-83/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد بمن كان حيا عاقلا وروي ذلك عن علي عليه السلام

TABRISI:36:66-69/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:66-69/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:66-69/r3.claim: Some read tunḏira as a direct address to the Prophet; others use yunḏira for the Quran or for God.
TABRISI:36:66-69/r3.anchor: ومن قرأ لتنذر بالتاء فهو خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن قرأ بالياء أراد القرآن

THALABI:v8p135#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p135#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p135#2/r5.claim: A person who is alive here is a rational believer in God's knowledge; unbelief and ignorance make the heart dead.
THALABI:v8p135#2/r5.anchor: من كان حيا أي عاقلا مؤمنا في علم الله لأن الكافر والجاهل ميت الفؤاد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:66-70/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:66-70/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:66-70/r5.claim: The reminder warns the intellectually living, since the disbeliever is like the dead, and establishes the case against disbelievers.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:66-70/r5.anchor: { لينذر من كان حيا } عاقلا، فلا يغفل ما يخاطب به؛ لأن الكافر كالميت

ELMALILI:36:68-76/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r9.claim: The Qur'an warns anyone truly alive, meaning one with reason and feeling, to awaken from heedlessness.
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r9.anchor: Hayâtı, yani aklı, duygusu olanı inzar edip gafletten uyandırmak

ELMALILI:36:68-76/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r10.claim: For those who persist in disbelief, the revealed word is fulfilled as a judgment of punishment becomes obligatory.
ELMALILI:36:68-76/r10.anchor: küfürde ısrar ile kâfirlik edenler aleyhine kavil hak olmak için bundan evvel ekserîsine olduğu gibi azab ile hüküm vâcib

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r6.claim: The closing section resumes the opening themes of monotheism and the Hereafter and assures the Prophet that he awakens the morally living, not the dead-hearted.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r6.anchor: what was discussed in the opening one is take up again in a different style

SAMIN-DURR:36:70/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:70/r1.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
SAMIN-DURR:36:70/r1.claim: Nafi and Ibn Amir read لتنذر in direct address here and in al-Ahqaf; others use third-person, with al-Bazzi differing in al-Ahqaf.
SAMIN-DURR:36:70/r1.anchor: قوله: { لينذر }: قرأ نافع وابن عامر هنا، في الأحقاف " لتنذر " خطابا. والباقون بالغيبة بخلاف عن البزي في الأحقاف

SAMIN-DURR:36:70/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:70/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:36:70/r2.claim: In the third-person reading, the pronoun may refer to the Prophet or the Quran.
SAMIN-DURR:36:70/r2.anchor: والغيبة تحتمل أن يكون الضمير فيها للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم. وأن تكون للقرآن.

SAMIN-DURR:36:70/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:36:70/r3.speaker: الجحدري واليماني
SAMIN-DURR:36:70/r3.claim: Al-Jahdari and al-Yamani read passively; Abu al-Simal and al-Yamani also read from نذر meaning to know, making من the subject.
SAMIN-DURR:36:70/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري واليماني " لينذر " مبنيا للمفعول. وأبو السمال واليماني أيضا " لينذر " بفتح الياء والذال

ZAJJAJ:v4p294/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p294/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p294/r1.claim: The implied subject of لينذر may be either the Prophet or the Qur’an.
ZAJJAJ:v4p294/r1.anchor: النبي عليه السلام. وجائز أن يكون القرآن

ZAJJAJ:v4p294/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p294/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p294/r2.claim: A living person here is one who understands what is addressed to him; a disbeliever is like the dead because he has not reflected and recognized the Prophet and his message as true.
ZAJJAJ:v4p294/r2.anchor: أي من كان يعقل ما يخاطب به، فإن الكافر كالميت

ZAJJAJ:v4p294/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p294/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p294/r3.claim: To make the word come due means to establish the proof against the disbelievers.
ZAJJAJ:v4p294/r3.anchor: ويجوز (ويحق القول)، أي يوجب الحجة عليهم.

ZAJJAJ:v4p294/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p294/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p294/r4.claim: The variant لتنذر uses second-person address to the Prophet.
ZAJJAJ:v4p294/r4.anchor: ويجوز لتنذر من كان حيا - بالتاء -

ZAJJAJ:v4p294/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p294/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p294/r5.claim: لينذر may also mean “to inform”; نذرت بكذا is used like علمت, “I knew.”
ZAJJAJ:v4p294/r5.anchor: ويجوز لينذر أي ليعلم، يقال نذرت بكذا وكذا،

ASAD-NOTES:36:69/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:36:69/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:36:69/r1.claim: Asad's gloss of the living as alive of heart signals spiritual responsiveness to the warning.
ASAD-NOTES:36:69/r1.anchor: warn everyone who is alive [of heart]

ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n40/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n40/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n40/r1.claim: The phrase means God's word will come or be proved true against deniers on Judgment Day, as indicated by 36:7.
ASAD-NOTES:36:69#n40/r1.anchor: Lit., "may come [or "be proved"] true", i.e., on the Day of Judgment

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p47/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p47/r1.speaker: نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p47/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ reads لتنذر with tāʾ, addressing the Prophet; the other readers have لينذر with yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p47/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع: لتنذر من كان حيا [يس/ 70] بالتاء وقرأ الباقون: لينذر بالياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p47/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p47/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p47/r2.claim: With yāʾ, the subject is the Qurʾān; the living are believers, while disbelievers are called dead, as in 16:21 and the revived man in 6:122.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p47/r2.anchor: ومن قال: ينذر*، أراد القرآن، ومعنى من كان حيا: من المؤمنين، لأن الكفار أموات

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p33/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p33/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p33/r1.claim: A reading’s weaker parsing or analogy does not invalidate it when it is transmitted from the early authorities; Ibn Jinnī says accepted readings among the Seven also include grammatically weak forms.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p33/r1.anchor: أكثر ما فيه أن يكون غيره من المجتمع عندهم عليه أقوى منه إعرابا وأنهض قياسا؛ إذ هما جميعا مرويان مسندان إلى السلف

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p33/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p33/r4.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p33/r4.claim: A widely transmitted and habitually received reading should not be set aside merely because a different reading has stronger grammar.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p33/r4.anchor: فأما أن نتوقف عن الأخذ به؛ لأن غيره أقوى إعرابا منه فلا؛ لما قدمنا

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p33/r5.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p33/r5.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p33/r5.claim: Ibn Jinnī aims to keep his argumentation accessible to readers of qirāʾāt; Abu ʿAlī’s al-Ḥujja goes beyond readers’ needs into material many scholars find difficult.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p33/r5.anchor: لا ننسى تقريبه على أهل القراءات؛ ليحظوا به، ولا ينأوا عن فهمه

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p33/r6.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p33/r6.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p33/r6.claim: Ibn Jinnī says Abu ʿAlī had once intended to write a book on readings but was prevented by the upheavals and distractions of the age.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p33/r6.anchor: هم أن يضع يده فيه، ويبدأ به، فاعترضت خوالج4 هذا الدهر دونه

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p33/r7.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p33/r7.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p33/r7.claim: Contrasting Abu ʿAlī’s quiet and freedom from worry with his own burdens, Ibn Jinnī says a sudden thought may still pierce distant veils, and he thanks God rather than complain.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p33/r7.anchor: ولعل الخطرة الواحدة تخرق بفكري أقصى الحجب المتراخية عني في جمع الشتات من أمري

NASHR:v2p354#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p354#2/r9.speaker: المدنيان وابن عامر ويعقوب
NASHR:v2p354#2/r9.claim: The two Medinans, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Yaʿqūb read the verb in direct address; the others use third person.
NASHR:v2p354#2/r9.anchor: فقرأ المدنيان، وابن عامر ويعقوب بالخطاب، وقرأ الباقون بالغيب

NASHR:v2p354#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p354#2/r10.speaker: رويس وروح
NASHR:v2p354#2/r10.claim: Ruways reads يقدر with open yāʾ, silent qāf, no alif, and nominative rāʾ here; Rawḥ agrees in al-Aḥqāf, while the others retain the alif form.
NASHR:v2p354#2/r10.anchor: فروى رويس (يقدر) بياء مفتوحة، وإسكان القاف من غير ألف وضم الراء

QIRAAT-ER:36:70:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:36:70:2#1/r1.speaker: Imp
QIRAAT-ER:36:70:2#1/r1.claim: The second-person imperfect means “so that you may warn,” making the addressee the explicit warner while retaining the purpose lām.
QIRAAT-ER:36:70:2#1/r1.anchor: Imp, mutawatir: "Canonical variant with second-person imperfect: ""so that you may warn""; the addressee becomes

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r8.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وباقي السبعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r8.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read لتنذر with second-person tāʾ, addressing the Prophet; the other seven read لينذر with third-person yāʾ, referring either to him or the Qur'an.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r8.anchor: وقرأ نافع، وابن عامر: لتنذر بتاء الخطاب للرسول وباقي السبعة: بالياء للغيبة، فاحتمل أن يعود على الرسول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r9.speaker: اليماني والجحدري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r9.claim: Al-Yamānī reads لينذر in the passive; Ibn Khalawayh transmits this reading from al-Jaḥdarī.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r9.anchor: وقرأ اليماني: لينذر، بالياء مبينا للمفعول، ونقلها ابن خالويه عن الجحدري.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r10.speaker: أبو السمال واليماني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r10.claim: Abū al-Sammāl and al-Yamānī read لينذر with fatḥa on yāʾ and dhāl, from نذر, meaning to learn of something and prepare for it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r10.anchor: وقال عن أبي السمال واليماني أنهما قرآ: لينذر، بفتح الياء والذال مضارع نذر بكسر الذال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r11.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r11.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk takes alive to mean heedless, since heedlessness resembles death; Abū Ḥayyān understands it as those decreed to have faith.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r11.anchor: من كان حيا: أي غافلا، قاله الضحاك، لأن الغافل كالميت ويريد به من حتم عليه بالإيمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r12.claim: The word that becomes due is the punishment against those destined to meet death persisting in disbelief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p81/r12.anchor: ويحق القول: أي كلمة العذاب، على الكافرين المحتوم لهم بالموافاة على الكفر.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r1.speaker: ابن الحاجب
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r1.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib argues that it would be irrational for the Prophet to compose poetry, since people might suspect revelation came from his own poetic faculty; removal of doubt leaves only their obstinacy, so the judgment falls on disbelievers.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p47/r1.anchor: وقال ابن الحاجب : أي لا يستقيم عقلا أن يقول صلى الله عليه وسلم الشعر لأنه لو كان ممن يقوله

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r1.claim: The subject of 'to warn' may be either the Qurʾān or the Messenger; the second-person reading supports the Messenger as subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r1.anchor: أي القرآن أو الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام ويؤيده قراءة نافع وابن عامر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r2.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r2.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read li-tundhira, addressing the Prophet directly, which supports taking him as the one who warns.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r2.anchor: ويؤيده قراءة نافع وابن عامر ( لتنذر ) بتاء الخطاب

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r3.speaker: اليماني
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r3.claim: Al-Yamānī reads the verb in the passive; Ibn Khālawayh attributes this reading to al-Jaḥdarī.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ اليماني ( لينذر ) مبنيا للمفعول ونقلها ابن خالويه عن الجحدري

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r4.speaker: أبو السمال واليماني
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r4.claim: Abū al-Sammāl and al-Yamānī are also reported to read with fatḥa on yāʾ and dhāl, from nadhira bi-shayʾ, meaning to know or become aware of it.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r4.anchor: بفتح الياء والذال مضارع نذر بالشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r5.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī and al-Bayhaqī in Shuʿab al-Īmān transmit from al-Ḍaḥḥāk that 'alive' means rational.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r5.anchor: كما أخرج ذلك ابن جرير والبيهقي في شعب الإيمان عن الضحاك

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r6.claim: On the rational reading, the verse uses an explicit metaphor by likening intellect to life.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r6.anchor: وفيه استعارة مصرحة بتشبيه العقل بالحياة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r7.claim: Alternatively, 'alive' means a believer, by contrast with the disbelievers; this explicitly likens faith to life, or treats faith as the cause of eternal life.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r7.anchor: أو مؤمنا بقرينة مقابلته بالكافرين وفيه أيضا استعارة مصرحة لتشبيه الإيمان بالحياة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r8.claim: The past tense in kāna reflects what is already certain in God's knowledge; alternatives take it as future tense or as a prospective event cast as past, which al-Ālūsī dismisses.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r8.anchor: والمضي في ( كان ) باعتبار ما في علمه عز وجل لتحققه وقيل كان بمعنى يكون

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r9.claim: Warning is singled out for the living because they are the ones who benefit from it.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r9.anchor: وتخصيص الإنذار به لأنه المنتفع بذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r10.claim: The 'word' that becomes binding on the persistent disbelievers is the sentence of punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r10.anchor: الموسومين بهذا الوسم المصرين على الكفر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r11.claim: Contrasting the living with disbelievers suggests that those lacking life's effects, such as knowledge, are truly dead; the wording may also contain a hidden metaphor signaled by another metaphor.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r11.anchor: وفي إيرادهم بمقابلة من حيا إشعار بأنهم لخلوهم عن آثار الحياة وأحكامها كالمعرفة أموات في الحقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r12.claim: The warning clause returns to the sūra's opening purpose of warning a people whose fathers were not warned; the transition from resurrection to Qurʾān and warning is strikingly apt.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p49#3/r12.anchor: وكأنه جيء بقوله سبحانه : ( لينذر ) الخ رجوعا إلى ما بديء به السورة من قوله عز وجل : ( لتنذر قوما ما أنذر آباؤهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27#2/r1.speaker: أهل المدينة والشام ويعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27#2/r1.claim: Medinan and Syrian readers and Yaʿqūb read with tāʾ, addressing the warning to Muhammad; the form also occurs in al-Aḥqāf.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة والشام ويعقوب "لتنذر" بالتاء وكذلك في الأحقاف،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27#2/r2.speaker: الآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27#2/r2.claim: The other readers use yāʾ, making the Qur'an the one that warns.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بالياء أي لينذر القرآن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27#2/r3.claim: The living person is a believer with a living heart; an unbeliever is like a dead person because he does not reflect.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27#2/r3.anchor: يعني: مؤمنا حي القلب؛ لأن الكافر كالميت في أنه لا يتدبر ولا يتفكر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p27#2/r4.claim: The word of punishment and its proof become binding against unbelievers.

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:70-71/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:70-71/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:70-71/r1.claim: The warner is the Qur’an or Messenger; the second-person reading supports the latter.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:70-71/r1.anchor: القرآن أو الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:70-71/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:70-71/r2.speaker: نافع وابن عامر ويعقوب
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:70-71/r2.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Yaʿqūb read the verb with تاء.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:70-71/r2.anchor: قراءة نافع وابن عامر ويعقوب بالتاء

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:70-71/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:70-71/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:70-71/r3.claim: “Alive” means rational and discerning, since the heedless are dead, or a believer in God’s knowledge, since eternal life comes through faith; warning targets beneficiaries.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:70-71/r3.anchor: فإن الغافل كالميت، أو مؤمنا في علم الله تعالى

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:70-71/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:70-71/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:70-71/r4.claim: The binding statement is the sentence of punishment.

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:70-71/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:70-71/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:70-71/r5.claim: The unbelievers persist in disbelief; their opposition to the living implies they are truly dead for lack of proof and reflection.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:70-71/r5.anchor: المصرين على الكفر، وجعلهم في مقابلة من كان حيا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r1.claim: The purpose is for the Messenger to warn; the clear Qur'an has formed him, so he manifests it and his state calls every truly living person to believe.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r1.anchor: وكان الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم متخلقا به

BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r2.speaker: نافع وابن عامر ويعقوب
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r2.claim: These authorities read the verb with direct address, 'so that you warn'; al-Biqāʿī takes this as indicating that no one understands the Qur'an fully as the Prophet does.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r2.anchor: ويؤيده لفت الكلام في قراءة نافع وابن عامر ويعقوب بالخطاب إشارة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r3.claim: The living person is one with complete inward life that leads to everlasting life; such a person is in truth a believer even if outward signs initially suggest otherwise.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r3.anchor: كونا متمكنا { حيا } أي حياة كاملة معنوية

BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r4.claim: The singular for the living follows the word's grammatical form and hints at the few fortunate; the plural for disbelievers follows its meaning and signals the many wretched.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r4.anchor: وأفرد الضمير هنا على اللفظ إشارة إلى قلة السعداء

BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r5.claim: The word that becomes binding is punishment, and the disbelievers are those deeply rooted in disbelief, dead in reality though they appear alive.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r5.anchor: أي يجب ويثبت { القول } أي بالعذاب

BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r6.claim: The verse uses ellipsis by reciprocal implication: faith is omitted from the first clause because its opposite appears in the second, and death is omitted from the second because its opposite appears in the first.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r6.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : حذف الإيمان أولا لما دل عليه من ضده ثانيا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r7.claim: The Qur'an's governing aim is serious meaning, with words following it; poets and rhymers put rhyme and cadence first, which can produce weak or false meanings.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r7.anchor: أن أعظم منافاة القرآن للشعر وكذا السجع من أجل أنه جد كله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r8.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r8.claim: At the expedition of al-Ghāba, Ḥassān's rhyming verse angered Saʿd ibn Zayd al-Ashhalī, who gave his horses to al-Miqdād and swore not to speak to him; Ḥassān explained the rhyme had forced the name.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r8.anchor: قال حسان بن ثابت رضي الله عنه وحاله معروف في البلاغة والتفنن في أساليب الكلام

BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r9.claim: The Prophet never chooses wording merely for polish or meter; he avoids a metrical option when it fails to convey the intended meaning, just as Arabs avoid grammatical error because it is error.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p280/r9.anchor: فالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يدور في فكره أبدا قصد اللفظ

DURR-FULL:v7p71/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p71/r5.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v7p71/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk explains “alive” as rational or intelligent.
DURR-FULL:v7p71/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك رضي الله عنه في قوله {لينذر من كان حيا} قال: عاقلا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200#2/r2.claim: Qatada says Muhammad was protected from poetry; the reminder is the Quran, intended to warn the living, meaning those alive in heart and sight, while the word takes effect against unbelievers through their evil deeds.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3200#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : وما علمناه الشعر وما ينبغي له قال : محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ، عصمه الله من ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r10.speaker: نافع وابن كثير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r10.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr read li-tundhira with tāʾ, addressing Muḥammad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r10.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير، «لتنذر» بالتاء على مخاطبة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r11.speaker: الباقون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r11.claim: The remaining readers use the yāʾ reading li-yundhira, referring either to the Qur'an or Muḥammad; the lām attaches to mubīn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r11.anchor: وقرأ الباقون «لينذر» بالياء أي لينذر القرآن أو لينذر محمد، واللام في «لينذر» متعلقة ب مبين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r12.speaker: محمد اليماني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r12.claim: Muḥammad al-Yamānī reads li-yundhira with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the dhāl; Abū Ḥātim says a passive reading with both vowels fatḥa would also be valid, meaning to be warned and take one's share, and Abū ʿAmr transmits it from him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r12.anchor: وقرأ محمد اليماني «لينذر» بضم الياء وفتح الذال قال أبو حاتم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r13.claim: The living person is one alive in heart and insight, not dead through disbelief; this is metaphorical. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses the phrase as rational.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r13.anchor: من كان حيا أي حي القلب والبصيرة، ولم يكن ميتا لكفره، وهذه استعارة قال الضحاك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r14.claim: Yaḥiqqa al-qawl means that punishment becomes certain and everlasting punishment obligatory.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p461/r14.anchor: ويحق القول معناه يحتم العذاب ويجب الخلود

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read liyundhira with yāʾ, referring to the Qurʾān.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي لينذر بالياء يعنون القرآن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r2.speaker: نافع وابن عامر ويعقوب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r2.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Yaʿqūb read litundhira with tāʾ, addressing the Prophet.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر ويعقوب لتنذر بالتاء يعنون النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r3.speaker: أبو المتوكل وأبو الجوزاء وابن السميفع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r3.claim: Abū al-Mutawakkil, Abū al-Jawzāʾ, and Ibn al-Sumayfaʿ read with a nominative yāʾ and fatḥa on the dhāl and rāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو المتوكل وأبو الجوزاء وابن السميفع لينذر بياء مرفوعة وفتح الذال والراء جميعا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r4.claim: Qatāda interprets the living person as one alive in heart and sight.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r4.anchor: أحدها حي القلب حي البصر قاله قتاده

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r5.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the living person is rational; al-Zajjāj explains that he understands the address, whereas an unbeliever is like the dead for rejecting warning.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r5.anchor: والثاني من كان عاقلا قاله الضحاك قال الزجاج من كان يعقل ما يخاطب به فان الكافر كالميت في ترك النذير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r6.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r6.claim: Al-Suddī interprets the living person as one who is guided.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r7.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r7.claim: Muqātil says it means one whom God knows to be guided.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r7.anchor: وقال مقاتل من كان مهتديا في علم الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r8.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r8.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Sallām interprets the living person as a believer, in keeping with the statement that only those who fear God are warned.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r8.anchor: والرابع من كان مؤمنا قاله يحيى بن سلام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r9.claim: The phrase may mean that warning benefits only someone who is a believer in God’s knowledge, and it echoes the earlier statement about those who fear their Lord.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p37#2/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد إنما ينفع إنذارك من كان مؤمنا في علم الله

BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r1.claim: The purpose phrase attaches either to Qur'an or to an implied verb supplied by reminder and Qur'an: they were revealed to warn.
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r1.anchor: أي : القرآن متعلق بقوله وقرآن أو بمحذوف دل عليه قوله إلا ذكر وقرآن

BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r2.claim: The living person is intelligent and discerning, uses the heart for its intended purpose, and benefits from reason as the body benefits from life; the heedless is like the dead.
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r2.anchor: أي : عاقلا فهيما يميز المصلحة من المفسدة ويستخدم قلبه فيما خلق له ولا يضيعه فيما لا يعنيه

BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r3.claim: A heart enlivened by God's light and spirit receives warning; its response is turning from this world toward the afterlife and its Lord.
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r3.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن كل قلب تكون حياته بنور الله وروح منه يفيده الإنذار ويتأثر به

BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r4.claim: Alive can mean a believer in God's knowledge: faith is life because it causes everlasting life.
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : من كان حيا أي : مؤمنا في علم الله فإن الحياة الأبدية بالإيمان

BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r5.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r5.claim: Ibn Ata says God gives life to one alive in His knowledge by looking toward him, letting him understand and hear from Him, and greeting him.
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : من كان في علم الله حيا أحياه الله بالنظر إليه والفهم عنه والسماع منه

BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r6.speaker: الجنيد
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r6.claim: Junayd defines the living as one whose life is through the Creator rather than the persistence of the self; life in God becomes real at death and reaches original life.
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r6.anchor: وقال الجنيد : الحي من كان حياته بحياة خالقه لا من تكون حياته ببقاء نفسه

BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r7.claim: Warning addresses both living and dead hearts, but only the living heart benefits from it.
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r7.anchor: وتخصيص الإنذار بمن كان حي القلب مع أنه عام له ولمن كان ميت القلب لأنه المنتفع به

BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r8.claim: The due word is the sentence that God will fill Hell with jinn and people; it falls on those persisting in unbelief.
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r8.anchor: أي : يجب كلمة العذاب وهو {لأملأن جهنم من الجنة والناس أجمعين}

BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r9.claim: Once doubt is removed and only obstinate opposition remains, punishment is due; unbelievers are truly dead like embryos before the spirit, while gnosis leads to faith, Islam, and excellence, whose people pass between places rather than die.
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r9.anchor: لأنه إذا انتفت الريبة إلا المعاندة فيحق القول عليهم وفي إيرادهم بمقابلة من كان حيا إشعار بأنهم لخلوهم عن آثار الحياة

BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r10.speaker: حضرة شيخي وسندي
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r10.claim: The shaykh reads sleep and waking as heedlessness and inner vigilance, waking as the heart's first awakening, ablution as repentance, and prayer as turning to God and entering the spiritual realm; movements carry blessings.
BURSEVI:v7p337#2/r10.anchor: حضرة شيخي وسندي روح الله روحه : حالة النوم وحالة الانتباه إشارة إلى الغفلة ويقظة البصيرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p592/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p592/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p592/r3.claim: The clear Qur'an warns every living being on earth, as in 6:19 and 11:17.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p592/r3.anchor: ولهذا قال: {لينذر من كان حيا} أي: لينذر هذا القرآن البين كل حي على وجه الأرض، كقوله: {لأنذركم به ومن بلغ}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p592/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p592/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p592/r4.claim: Qatada interprets the living person as alive in heart and sight.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p592/r4.anchor: كما قال قتادة: حي القلب، حي البصر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p592/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p592/r5.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p592/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets alive as possessing reason.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p592/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p592/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p592/r6.claim: The warning also establishes that whoever among the groups disbelieves will have Hell as their appointed destination.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p592/r6.anchor: وقال: {ومن يكفر به من الأحزاب فالنار موعده}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p592/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p592/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p592/r7.claim: The Qur'an is mercy for the believer and a conclusive proof against the disbeliever.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p592/r7.anchor: هو رحمة للمؤمن، وحجة على الكافر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p28#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p28#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p28#2/r9.claim: The subject of “that he may warn” may be the Qur’an or the Messenger.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p28#2/r9.anchor: لينذر } القرآن أو الرسول وقرىء : ( لتنذر ) بالتاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p28#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p28#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p28#2/r10.claim: A variant reads li-tundhira in the second person, addressing the Prophet.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p28#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p28#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p28#2/r11.claim: The verb nadhara bihi can mean to know or become informed of something.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p28#2/r11.anchor: ولينذر : من نذر به إذا علمه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p28#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p28#2/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p28#2/r12.claim: The living person reasons, since the heedless are like the dead; alternatively, it means one known to believe and live by faith.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p28#2/r12.anchor: أي عاقلا متأملا ، لأن الغافل كالميت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p28#2/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p28#2/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p28#2/r13.claim: The statement of punishment becomes binding on disbelievers who do not reflect and are not expected to believe.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p28#2/r13.anchor: وتجب كلمة العذاب { على الكافرين } الذي لا يتأملون ولا يتوقع منهم الإيمان

MUQATIL:36:70/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:70/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:70/r1.claim: Muhammad is to warn people with the Qur’an’s threats.
MUQATIL:36:70/r1.anchor: يعنى لتنذر يا محمد بما فى القرآن من الوعيد

MUQATIL:36:70/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:70/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:70/r2.claim: The living person is someone whom God knows to be guided.
MUQATIL:36:70/r2.anchor: من كان حيا } من كان مهديا في علم الله

MUQATIL:36:70/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:70/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:70/r3.claim: The word due upon unbelievers is punishment for rejecting God’s oneness.
MUQATIL:36:70/r3.anchor: ويجب العذاب { على الكافرين } [آية: 70] بتوحيد الله عز وجل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p13#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p13#3/r1.speaker: مدني وشامي وسهل ويعقوب
NASAFI-FULL:v4p13#3/r1.claim: These readers have the second-person reading litundhira, addressed to the Prophet; the alternative subject is the Qur'an or the Messenger.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p13#3/r1.anchor: القرآن أو الرسول لتنذر مدني وشامي وسهل ويعقوب

NASAFI-FULL:v4p13#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p13#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p13#3/r2.claim: The living person is one who reasons and reflects; the heedless is like the dead. It can also mean one alive in heart.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p13#3/r2.anchor: عاقلا متأملا لأن الغافل كالميت أو حيا بالقلب

NASAFI-FULL:v4p13#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p13#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p13#3/r3.claim: The word of punishment becomes binding against disbelievers who do not reflect and are therefore counted among the dead.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p13#3/r3.anchor: وتجب كلمة العذاب ﴿ على الكافرين ﴾ الذين لا يتأملون وهم في حكم الاموات

QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r10.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r10.claim: Qatada takes the living person to mean one whose heart is alive.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r11.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r11.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the living person as a rational person.

QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r12.claim: Another interpretation is that the warning reaches whoever is a believer in God’s knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r12.anchor: وقيل: المعنى لتنذر من كان مؤمنا في علم الله

QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r13.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r13.claim: Nafi and Ibn Amir read with second-person ta, addressing the Prophet: that he may warn.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r13.anchor: قراءة التاء خطابا للنبي عليه السلام، وهي قراءة نافع وابن عامر

QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r14.speaker: الباقون
QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r14.claim: The other readers use yā; the subject may be God, Muhammad, or the Qur’an.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r14.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالياء على معنى لينذر الله عز وجل أو لينذر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، أو لينذر القرآن

QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r15.speaker: ابن السميقع
QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r15.claim: Ibn al-Sumayqa is also reported to read the form with fatḥa on yā and dhāl.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r15.anchor: وروي عن ابن السميقع «لينذر» بفتح الياء والذال

QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:69-70#4/r16.claim: The Qur’an makes the proof binding against the unbelievers.

RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r1.claim: The verb has a tāʾ reading that addresses Muhammad and a yāʾ reading that is either about Muhammad or the Qur'an; the former yāʾ interpretation is closer in meaning and the latter closer in wording.
RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r1.anchor: خطابا مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وبالياء على وجهين

RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r2.claim: With yāʾ, the Prophet can be the one warning, referring back to him in the preceding verses; al-Razi judges this closer in meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r2.anchor: أن يكون المنذر هو النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حيث سبق ذكره

RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r3.claim: Alternatively, the Qur'an itself can be the subject of “warn”; this reading is closer to the wording because the Qur'an is the nearest antecedent.
RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r3.anchor: أن يكون المراد أن القرآن ينذر

RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r4.claim: “Alive” may mean alive in God's knowledge, destined to be guided by the warning.
RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r4.anchor: من كان حيا في علم الله فينذره به فيؤمن

RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r5.claim: Alternatively, it means alive in reality, that is, a believer who is warned of punishment for sins and reward for obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r5.anchor: لينذر به من كان حيا في نفس الأمر

RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r6.claim: “The word becomes due” can mean God's sentence of punishment after a messenger has come, including the decree to fill Hell; punishment then falls on those who denied the messenger.
RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r6.anchor: أما قول العذاب وكلمته كما قال تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r7.claim: Alternatively, it refers to the statements about oneness, prophethood, resurrection, and the other foundational doctrines, whose proofs the Qur'an provides.
RAZI-FULL:v26p93/r7.anchor: وأما القول المقول في الوحدانية والرسالة والحشر

STUDYQURAN:36:70/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:70/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:36:70/r1.claim: IK takes warning those who are alive to mean all humanity, as in the Quran’s warning to its hearers and whomever it reaches.
STUDYQURAN:36:70/r1.anchor: all of humanity, as in 6:19: And this Quran has been revealed unto me, that thereby I may warn you and whomsoever it may reach (IK)

STUDYQURAN:36:70/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:70/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:36:70/r2.claim: Q takes those who are alive as people whose hearts live and can hear the warning and soften at God’s remembrance.
STUDYQURAN:36:70/r2.anchor: those whose hearts are alive (Q) and thus able to hear the warning and soften unto the remembrance of God (39:23)

STUDYQURAN:36:70/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:70/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:36:70/r3.claim: For the meaning of the Word coming due for disbelievers, the commentary refers to 36:7.
STUDYQURAN:36:70/r3.anchor: For the meaning of the Word coming due, see 36:7c.

TAB-FULL:v19p481/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p481/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p481/r1.claim: Muhammad warns the living-hearted, who can reason and understand what is said, unlike the dull and dead-hearted.
TAB-FULL:v19p481/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {لينذر من كان حيا} [يس: 70] «حي القلب، حي البصر»

TAB-FULL:v19p481/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p481/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v19p481/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: {لينذر من كان حيا} [يس: 70] قال: «من كان عاقلا»

TAB-FULL:v19p481/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p481/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p481/r3.claim: Qatada describes the living as alive in heart and sight.
TAB-FULL:v19p481/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {لينذر من كان حيا} [يس: 70] «حي القلب، حي البصر»

TAB-FULL:v19p482/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p482/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p482/r1.claim: Punishment becomes due on those who disbelieve, turn away from following God, and reject what He brought.

TAB-FULL:v19p482/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p482/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p482/r2.claim: Qatada says punishment becomes due because of their deeds.

SULAMI:v2p175/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p175/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p175/r1.claim: God gives life to those known to Him as living by enabling them to behold, understand, hear, and receive greeting from Him.
SULAMI:v2p175/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أي من كان في علم الله حيا احياه الله بالنظر إليه

SULAMI:v2p175/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p175/r2.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v2p175/r2.claim: The message is delivered to those for whom God has already ordained His gift.
SULAMI:v2p175/r2.anchor: قال جعفر : ليبلغ الرسالة إلى من سبقت له من الله العطية

SULAMI:v2p175/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p175/r3.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p175/r3.claim: The truly living draw life from their Creator, not bodily survival; one sustained only by the self is dead while alive, whereas life through God is realized at death as the original life.
SULAMI:v2p175/r3.anchor: قال الجنيد - رحمة الله عليه - : الحي : من تكون حياته بحياة خالقه

TABATABAI:36:69-71/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:69-71/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:69-71/r4.claim: The purpose clause may attach either to God's not teaching the Prophet poetry or to the statement that what he recites is only reminder and clear Quran; both readings yield the same meaning.
TABATABAI:36:69-71/r4.anchor: تعليل متعلق بقوله { وما علمناه الشعر } والمعنى ولم نعلمه الشعر لينذر

TABATABAI:36:69-71/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:69-71/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:69-71/r5.claim: Being alive is a metaphor for understanding the truth and hearing it.
TABATABAI:36:69-71/r5.anchor: وهو كناية عن كونه يعقل الحق ويسمعه

TABATABAI:36:69-71/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:69-71/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:69-71/r6.claim: The verse's purpose of warning the receptive and establishing the word against disbelievers echoes the opening of Sūrat Yā Sīn.
TABATABAI:36:69-71/r6.anchor: فمحاذاة الآية لما في صدر السورة من الآيات في هذا المعنى ظاهر

TABRISI:36:69-70/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:69-70/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:69-70/r3.claim: The revelation warns those alive in faith against disobeying God; an unbeliever is like the dead, or worse, since he gains no benefit from his religion and is harmed by it.
TABRISI:36:69-70/r3.anchor: أي أنزلناه لتخوف به من معاصي الله من كان مؤمنا لأن الكافر كالميت

TABRISI:36:69-70/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:69-70/r4.speaker: علي
TABRISI:36:69-70/r4.claim: Another explanation transmitted from ʿAli is that the living person is one with reason.
TABRISI:36:69-70/r4.anchor: المراد بمن كان حيا عاقلا وروي ذلك عن علي ع

TABRISI:36:69-70/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:69-70/r5.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:36:69-70/r5.claim: Qatada says “alive” means alive in heart and sight.
TABRISI:36:69-70/r5.anchor: حي القلب حي البصر عن قتادة

TABRISI:36:69-70/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:69-70/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:69-70/r6.claim: The threat and punishment become due upon unbelievers because of their unbelief.
TABRISI:36:69-70/r6.anchor: أي يجب الوعيد والعذاب على الكافرين بكفرهم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p368#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p368#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p368#3/r1.claim: One explanation takes “alive” to mean a believer.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p368#3/r1.anchor: لينذر من كان حيا} أي مؤمنا. ويقال: عاقلا.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p368#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p368#3/r2.speaker: غير مسمى
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p368#3/r2.claim: Another reported explanation takes “alive” to mean rational or intelligent.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r1.claim: With li-yundhira, the subject is the Qurʾān; readers who use the tāʾ address Muḥammad, who warns through the Qurʾān’s threats.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r1.anchor: {لينذر} أي: القرآن، ومن قرأ بالتاء فهو خطاب للنبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم-

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the living person is a believer.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r3.claim: Muqātil says it means someone whom God knows will be guided.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل: من كان مهتديا في علم الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r4.claim: Abū Isḥāq says it means someone capable of understanding what is addressed to him; a disbeliever is like a dead person and does not reflect.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: أي من يعقل ما يخاطب به، فإن الكافر كالميت، وإنه لا يتدبر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r5.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r5.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī identifies the living as believers because disbelievers are dead, citing 16:26 and 6:122.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r5.anchor: وقال أبو علي الفارسي: (يعني المؤمنين؛ لأن الكفار أموات كما قال {أموات غير أحياء}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r6.claim: The Qurʾān makes the proof binding against the disbelievers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p520#2/r6.anchor: وقوله: {ويحق القول} أي: ويجب الحجة بالقرآن على الكافرين

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p819/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p819/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p819/r1.claim: The warning is a warning of the Fire.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p819/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p819/r2.speaker: قارئو الياء
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p819/r2.claim: Those who read the verb with yāʾ take the Quran as the one warning.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p819/r2.anchor: من قرأها بالياء يقول لينذر القرآن،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p819/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p819/r3.speaker: قارئو التاء
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p819/r3.claim: Those who read the verb with tāʾ take the Prophet as the one warning.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p819/r3.anchor: ومن قرأها بالتاء يقول: لتنذر يا محمد.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p819/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p819/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p819/r4.claim: The one who is alive is a believer.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p819/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p819/r5.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p819/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says the living person is guided and a believer in God’s knowledge, and so accepts the Prophet’s warning.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p819/r5.anchor: وقال السدي: يعني: مهتديا، مؤمنا في علم الله، هو الذي يقبل نذارتك.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p819/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p819/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p819/r6.claim: The word qawl here means wrath.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:70/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:70/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:70/r1.claim: The spiritually, intellectually, and emotionally living are those who use reason and do not deliberately block faith; they can receive the Qur’an’s warnings.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:70/r1.anchor: Akıl nimetini gereğince değerlendirebilen ve iman ışığının gönlüne girmesini önlemek için özel bir çaba harcamayan yani basireti açık

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:70/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:70/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:70/r2.claim: Obstinate rejecters deserve punishment because they have no excuse; this fulfills God’s decree to fill Hell with those who follow Satan.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:70/r2.anchor: bağnaz biçimde inkârcılığa sarılanlar ise, –artık mazeretleri kalmayacağından– cezaya müstahak olacaklar, böylece şuurlu varlıkları yaratırken yüce Allah’ın belirlediği hüküm

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:70/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:70/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:70/r3.claim: The clause’s subject is usually understood as the Qur’an, though the implicit subject could instead be the Prophet.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:70/r3.anchor: İlk cümlenin öznesi genellikle Kur’an olarak düşünülmüştür; özne açık isim olmadığı için bunu “Peygamber uyarsın diye” şeklinde anlamak da mümkündür.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:70/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:70/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:70/r4.claim: A reading meaning “so that you may warn” is also reported; the change does not alter the expression’s essential meaning.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:70/r4.anchor: Ayrıca “uyarasın diye” anlamına gelen bir kıraat de vardır. Fakat her iki duruma göre ifadenin özünde bir değişiklik olmamaktadır

BAQILLANI:v1p134/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p134/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p134/r1.claim: Bāqillānī reproduces a letter from Muhammad, Messenger of God, to Chosroes, great king of Persia. It invites him to Islam and uses the warning that the revelation addresses the living and confirms judgment against disbelievers.
BAQILLANI:v1p134/r1.anchor: من محمد رسول الله إلى كسرى عظيم فارس سلام على من اتبع الهدى وآمن بالله ورسوله

BURHAN:v1p453/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p453/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p453/r3.claim: The beloved's speech gives life to hearts: only a living person is warned by it, and only one who responds comes alive through it, linking the warning verse with the call to what gives life.
BURHAN:v1p453/r3.anchor: لأن كلام المحبوب حياة للقلوب لا ينذر به إلا حى ولا يحيا به إلا مستجيب

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r1.claim: A metaphor replaces the word for one item with the word for another; صاغ الربيع and حاك الربيع name only one agent and therefore cannot be analyzed as a simile of a thing to itself.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r1.anchor: وكان معنى الاستعارة أن تغير لفظ المشبه بلفظ المشبه به ولم يكن معنا في صاغ الربيع أو حاك الربيع إلا شيء واحد

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r2.claim: Spring's assignment the role of an agent reflects an unspoken conceptual analogy, not a simile expressed with كأن or كاف; the analogy lies in spring, not in the verb.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r2.anchor: وإنما هو عبارة عن الجهة التي راعاها المتكلم حين أعطى الربيع حكم القادر في إسناد الفعل إليه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r3.claim: The author distinguishes a spoken, stated simile from an analogy conceived in the speaker's reasoning but absent from the utterance.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r3.anchor: كلامنا إذن في تشبيه منقول منطوق به وأنت في تشبيه معقول غير داخل في النطق

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r4.claim: A clause is literal when its expressed judgment matches the judgment as reason conceives it and is free of interpretive transfer.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r4.anchor: فكل جملة وضعتها على أن الحكم المفاد بها على ما هو عليه في العقل وواقع موقعه فهي حقيقة ولن تكون كذلك حتى تعرى من التأول

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r5.claim: Literalness concerns how a judgment is expressed, not whether it is correct or truthful; a false assertion can still be literal.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r5.anchor: ولا فصل بين أن تكون مصيبا فيما أفدت بها من الحكم أو مخطئا وصادقا أو غير صادق

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r6.claim: God's creation of the world exemplifies truths firmly fixed in reason; the Qur'anic image of a fall from heaven illustrates the collapse of reason when such truths are denied.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p331/r6.anchor: ومن يشرك بالله فكأنما خر من السماء فتخطفه الطير أو تهوى به الريح في مكان سحيق

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p52/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p52/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p52/r1.claim: Rhetorical merit is the completeness and beauty of speech's indication of its intended meaning, presented in a form that more powerfully attracts the hearer.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p52/r1.anchor: غير وصف الكلام بحسن الدلالة وتمامها فيما له كانت دلالة ، ثم تبرجها

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p52/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p52/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p52/r2.claim: Good expression approaches the meaning in its most accurate way and chooses the word most specific, revealing, and complete for it, thereby showing its merit.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p52/r2.anchor: ولا جهة لاستعمال هذه الخصال غير أن يؤتى المعنى من الجهة التي هي أصح لتأديته

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p52/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p52/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p52/r3.claim: Isolated words do not differ in semantic clarity for the thing they name; outside composition, distinctions are familiarity versus strangeness or lighter, more fluent sounds, as with ليث and أسد.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p52/r3.anchor: أن تتفاضل الكلمتان المفردتان من غير أن ينظر إلى مكان تقعان فيه من التأليف والنظم

NAHHAS:v3p404/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p404/r6.speaker: أبو عبيد
NAHHAS:v3p404/r6.claim: The people of Medina read لتُنذر, which Abu Ubayd favors, citing إنما أنت منذر.
NAHHAS:v3p404/r6.anchor: هذه قراءة أهل المدينة ومال إليها أبو عبيد

NAHHAS:v3p404/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p404/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
NAHHAS:v3p404/r7.claim: Abu Amr and the Kufians read لينذر; its subject may be God, the Quran, or Muhammad.
NAHHAS:v3p404/r7.anchor: وقراءة أبي عمرو وأهل الكوفة ( لينذر ) يكون معناها لينذر الله جل وعز أو لينذر القرآن

NAHHAS:v3p404/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p404/r8.speaker: محمد بن السميفع اليماني
NAHHAS:v3p404/r8.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Sumayfa al-Yamani also reads لينذر من كان حيا.
NAHHAS:v3p404/r8.anchor: وقرأ محمد بن السميفع اليماني لينذر من كان حيا

NAHHAS:v3p404/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p404/r9.speaker: الضحاك
NAHHAS:v3p404/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak says the living person is a believer, alive in the sense of accepting what benefits him.
NAHHAS:v3p404/r9.anchor: قال جويبر عن الضحاك من كان حيا أي من كان مؤمنا أي لأن المؤمن بمنزلة الحي

NAHHAS:v3p404/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p404/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p404/r10.claim: The punishment statement becomes binding on unbelievers because of their unbelief; another parse takes it to mean proof is established against them.
NAHHAS:v3p404/r10.anchor: أي يحق عليهم أن الله جل وعز يعذبهم وإنما يحق عليهم هذا بعد كفرهم

NAHHAS:v3p404/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p404/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p404/r11.claim: Some grammarians derive تنذر from نذرت بالقوم, meaning to learn of people and prepare for them.
NAHHAS:v3p404/r11.anchor: من قولهم نذرت بالقوم أنذر إذا علمت بهم فاستعددت لهم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r4.claim: A third sense is guidance: the guided person is described as alive.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p253/r4.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الحياة في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p409/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p409/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p409/r1.claim: After explaining who will benefit from the Book, the closing passage points to providential signs that call for gratitude, then reassures the Prophet to entrust opponents’ mockery to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p409/r1.anchor: some very prominent signs of God’s providence are alluded to in order to once again invite people to show gratitude to God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p412/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p412/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p412/r3.claim: The subject of “that it may warn” is the Prophet Muhammad.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p412/r3.anchor: The subject of the verb َرِنذُی is the Prophet Muh@ammad (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p412/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p412/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p412/r4.claim: The Qur’an was revealed to warn the intellectually and spiritually alive; those with dead hearts will not benefit, but the truth is conveyed conclusively so disbelievers have no excuse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p412/r4.anchor: the truth shall stand conclusively conveyed to them and they will not be able to present this excuse before God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p412/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p412/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p412/r5.claim: Warning has its full force for people whose hearts are alive and responsive; Islahi cites 36:11 and 35:22 to contrast those who heed with the spiritually dead.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p412/r5.anchor: The verb انذار warning) here is in its complete meaning and the word ّيَحٌ refers to those whose hearts are alive.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p412/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p412/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p412/r6.claim: The verse’s phrasing reassures the Prophet that his task is to awaken the living, not the spiritually dead, a recurring Qur’anic theme.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p412/r6.anchor: The style adopted in the verse under discussion sounds an assurance to the Prophet (sws) as well.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p412/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p412/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p412/r7.claim: The conclusive “word” against disbelievers refers to God’s earlier promise to reveal guidance to Adam’s progeny and punish those who follow Satan despite it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p412/r7.anchor: the truth shall stand conclusively conveyed to them and they will not be able to present this excuse before God

JISHUMI:v8p5899/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5899/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5899/r7.claim: Warning through the Quran benefits those who listen, not those who turn away from it.
JISHUMI:v8p5899/r7.anchor: وتدل أن الإنذار بالقرآن يقع لمن يستمع دون المعرض عنه

DAMGHANI:v1p150/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p150/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p150/r2.claim: Al-ḥayy can mean a believer guided in God’s knowledge; related examples describe guidance and distinguish believers from unbelievers.
DAMGHANI:v1p150/r2.anchor: الثاني : الحي يعني المؤمن المهتدي قوله تعالى في سورة يس
